prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” interior painting company for all situations in St. Louis — the right painter depends on your neighborhood, budget, project size, timing, and whether you need specialty work (trim, high ceilings, cabinets, stain work, texture repair, etc.). I can help you find the best match. To get you started, here’s a practical plan and checklist so you can identify the best local contractor for your job.

How to find the best interior painter in St. Louis
- Check multiple review sources: Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, Houzz, and the BBB. Read recent reviews and look for consistency (quality + punctuality + cleanup).
- Ask neighbors or local Facebook/Nextdoor groups for firsthand referrals.
- Get at least 3 written estimates and compare them line-by-line.
- Look for experience with interiors similar to yours (older homes vs. modern condos, high ceilings, trim/cabinet work).

Must-have credentials and protections
- General liability insurance and workers’ comp.
- Local business license (if required).
- Written contract with scope, paint brands and sheens, number of coats, prep work, timeline, payment schedule, and warranty/guarantee.

Questions to ask every painter
- Do you provide a written estimate? What’s included/excluded?
- Which paint brand and finish do you recommend and why?
- How many coats, and how will you handle prep (patching, sanding, priming)?
- Will you protect floors/furniture and clean daily?
- Do you provide color consultation?
- Can I see before/after photos and references of similar jobs?
- What is your timeline and payment schedule?

What a fair estimate should include
- Detailed line items for labor, materials, primer, number of coats.
- Prep work (patching, caulking, sanding, priming).
- Trim/ceiling costs listed separately if applicable.
- Cleanup and final walkthrough included.

Red flags to avoid
- Very low bids with pressure for immediate signing.
- No insurance or no written contract.
- Vague scope (“we’ll paint everything”) with no specifics on coats or prep.
- Poor or no references and few online reviews.

Typical price check (ballpark)
- Expect variation by home size and complexity. For most interiors, painters often charge by the room, by the hour, or by square footage. Get multiple bids — price alone shouldn’t be the deciding factor.

If you want, I can:
- Recommend 3–5 highly rated painters in your immediate area if you tell me your ZIP code, type of property, and roughly how many rooms or square feet.
- Provide a sample email or script to request estimates.
- Walk you through comparing three bids you receive.

Which would you like to do next?
